note: Real-AWS demo of 2026-11-17 (infra/README.md section 8). Exported read-only from the local SQLite store; the instance id is left out. The same incident was investigated with prompt investigation-v1 (high-confidence causal claim from two co-occurring breaches) and, after the reliability fix, investigation-v2. F1's statement says 13:10 UTC for a window that starts at 12:10 UTC: a collector time-zone bug found by this run and fixed afterwards (stored facts are append-only, so it stays here).

facts.statement: CPU credit balance at or below 5 credits for 15 min since 13:10 UTC (lowest 0.0 credits)
5xx error rate at or above 5% for 11 min since 12:11 UTC (peak 21.1%)
EC2 status check passing at the latest datapoint

findings.summary: CPU credits dropped to zero and 5xx errors spiked, suggesting CPU throttling caused the errors.

hypotheses.statement: CPU credit exhaustion caused CPU throttling, leading to 5xx errors.
5xx errors were caused by an unrelated application issue.

next_checks.description: Review CPU credit usage trend and instance type to confirm throttling.
Examine application logs around 12:11‑12:22 UTC for error patterns.

remediation.description: Upgrade the instance to a higher CPU credit balance or enable unlimited mode to prevent future throttling.
Add horizontal scaling to distribute load and reduce 5xx spikes.

limitations: No application logs or detailed CPU usage data are available to confirm the exact cause of the 5xx errors.
